findings.detail: The row's bold lead still reads "the OCR → Rewaa branch (`ocr-rewaa-parity`, `d82c459`, not yet merged)" while the `Blocked by` cell this PR rewrote now says "`ocr-rewaa-parity` was merged and deployed on 2026-09-30 (`8c28064`) and the branch deleted." Both statements are in the same table row. A reader triaging TD-055 cannot tell from this row whether the prerequisite branch is still in flight — which is exactly the question the `Blocked by` edit was made to answer. The register is the artifact people consult instead of git, so a stale clause inside it re-creates the archaeology it exists to prevent.
findings.summary: TD-055 row contradicts itself on whether ocr-rewaa-parity was merged

findings.detail: `git log -1 8c28064` is `evidence: gate green for 3ef252f (11/11, AI review APPROVED, 1 medium open)` — an evidence record dated 2026-09-30 on `main`. The commit that actually landed the OCR → Rewaa work is its parent `3ef252f` ("OCR → Rewaa: output matches the supplied correct file; auto-download and ZIP"). Citing the evidence commit as the thing that was "merged and deployed" sends anyone who follows the SHA to a gate receipt rather than to the change. Both commits are on `main`, so nothing is wrong — only imprecise.
findings.summary: `8c28064` is the evidence commit, not the branch's work commit

findings.detail: The new pointer `[\`open-decisions.md\` D12 rule 7](../modules/open-decisions.md)` resolves correctly to `docs/modules/open-decisions.md`, but with no fragment the reader arrives at line 1 and has to scan to the D12 heading at line 271 and then to row 7 of its table. The whole point of the restructure is that TD-055 delegates to D12 rule 7, so the handoff is worth making one click rather than one search. The D12 heading is bilingual with em-dashes, which makes a generated anchor fragile — an explicit anchor is the stable fix.
findings.summary: Link to D12 rule 7 has no anchor and lands at the top of a ~300-line doc
